language.script_notes: Latin alphabet with æ, ø, å. The ø (shared with Danish, not Swedish) is the quick separator from Swedish ö. Two written standards, Bokmål and Nynorsk. Road-name suffixes -veien / -vegen and -gate. .no domain. Northern Sámi also appears on signs in the far north.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Black and white when present, but roadside bollards are uncommon in Norway.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Flat-faced post; not a reliable feature because they appear so rarely.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Standard steel W-beam. Frequent road tunnels, avalanche sheds and rock cuttings are a stronger Norway signal than the guardrail itself.
road_furniture.line_paint: YELLOW centre line with white edge lines — the single most reliable Norway tell among the Nordics (Sweden uses white). Edge-line dashes are long, the longest in Scandinavia.
road_furniture.curb_style: No strongly distinctive curb style noted.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Wooden utility poles. Tall reflector-topped snow poles line many roads, sometimes with an orange band lower down; slim metal pipe/cable markers also occur.

architecture.roof_style: Gabled roofs; traditional turf/sod roofs appear on rural and heritage buildings.
architecture.roof_material: Clay tile, sheet metal and slate (slate more in the west); occasional grass-covered turf roofs.
architecture.wall_construction: Painted timber panelling is dominant outside city centres.
architecture.wall_color_palette: White, Falu red and ochre; brightly painted wooden houses cluster around harbours (e.g. Bergen).
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Red and white wooden houses; rorbuer (fishermen's cabins, often on stilts over water) in Lofoten; a handful of stave churches; turf-roofed farm buildings.

nature.vegetation: Broadleaf and mixed woodland along the milder south coast; conifer forest inland; sparse birch and bare tundra at altitude and in the far north.
nature.terrain: Very mountainous, cut by deep fjords and steep valleys. Dramatic relief, hairpin roads, countless islands and long coastline — terrain alone often separates Norway from flatter Sweden and Finland.
nature.climate_signature: Snow and snow poles are common. The west coast is frequently wet and overcast; areas north of the Arctic Circle have very dark winters and midnight sun in summer.

vehicles.plate_color: White with a blue strip carrying the Norwegian flag and 'N' — blue tag but NO EU stars, since Norway is outside the EU. Green plates mark commercial/goods vehicles.
vehicles.plate_format: Two letters then five digits (e.g. AB 12345).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: An unusually high proportion of electric cars (Teslas, e-Golfs and similar) thanks to strong EV incentives — a genuine Norway signal. Green commercial plates on vans.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of Gen 2 and Gen 3 (no visible car) and Gen 4 (car visible).
google_coverage.blur_style: Standard Google blurring, nothing unusual noted.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: White Google car when visible (Gen 4). Coverage includes many tunnels, mountain passes and snowy roads; some remote fjord roads are ferry-linked.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Falu-red timber houses, Latin script with extra vowels, snowy conifer landscapes, wooden poles, near-identical plates at a glance
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Norway has a YELLOW centre line and long edge-line dashes; Sweden's centre line is white. Norway uses ø, Sweden ö. Norway is mountainous with fjords and tunnels; central/southern Sweden is flat.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Scandinavian language, similar signage and plates
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Denmark is flat farmland with no mountains, no snow poles and no tunnels, and uses ø like Norway but has a completely different landscape and denser road network.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Snow-heavy Nordic coverage, conifer forest, wooden poles
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Finnish text is unmistakable and unlike Norwegian. Finland is flat with endless lakes and forest; Norway is steep and fjord-cut. Finnish bollards look cylindrical.
